items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The Montgomery brothers were – we were very – in fact they were very influential to us, because they were very far in advance of us.

ctx.x: The Montgomery brothers were – we were very – in fact they were very influential to us, because they were very far in advance of us. They had their own thing that they practiced and worked together. They were – they didn’t play music by the theory that they had learned. They played by what they heard. So they were much further advanced in theory and all that, and that’s because they didn’t have any rules that they had to go by. They just had to make the music sound the way that they thought it should sound. They…

Could you tell us a little bit about the family band’s repertoire and the kinds of places that you played? I imagine that you weren’t participating when you got to Middletown, at four. When did you first become a part of the family band?
